Washington Wildfires Scorch 250,000 Acres, Trigger Evacuations and Power Outages

Wildfires in Washington state burned over 250,000 acres, prompting evacuations and power outages. The fires were reported to have started on July 28th. State officials said the wildfires had led to widespread evacuations and power outages. The US Forest Service claimed that the fires were being closely monitored by firefighters. The National Weather Service warned of continued hot and dry conditions. Washington state Governor Jay Inslee declared a state of emergency.
